newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-KLM to sell Northwest stake, tighten links.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-KLM to sell Northwest stake, tighten links.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Wednesday it would sell its shares in Northwest Airlines to strengthen their operational alliance, soothing the U.S. carrier's fears it was out to gain control.
"KLM and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines have agreed in principle on a far-reaching and long-term commercial and operational alliance," the airlines said in a joint statement.

"The agreement in principle also includes the sale of the entire KLM stake in Northwest to Northwest Airlines Corporation (NWAC). KLM will be paid a minimum of $1.07 billion and a maximum of $1.17 billion," the statement said.
"The agreement clears the way for further strengthening of the partnership, which continues to be very successful for both companies," it added.
KLM's 18.8 percent voting stake in Northwest will be sold off in four annual tranches from 1997 to 2000.

KLM and Northwest have been locked in a boardroom battle, with KLM taking the U.S. carrier to court over its shareholder rights plan to prevent KLM gaining a further five percent stake under an option exercisable in 1998.
Northwest has repeatedly charged KLM with seeking to take over, labelling the Dutch carrier "a creeping control threat".
The airlines said in their statement that they planned to finalise a definitive agreement within 60 days and KLM would subsequently withdraw pending legal actions.

KLM said its partnership with Northwest continued to be successful for both carriers and, to stress the importance of strengthening the alliance each partner intended to appoint a person to each other's board, it said.

The airlines are to commit themselves to a commercial and operational relationship for a minimum of ten years, building further strategies for joint marketing and product development and pursue the further widening of their alliance with new partners.
Shares in airline KLM jumped 2.60 guilders to 75.00 following the stake sale news.
"The shares have gone up because there will be a book profit from the stake sales, but whether this is good for KLM in the longer term isn't that clear," said a dealer.
